inputs.obligation_targeted: 15 obligations across ORA-WRITE-001, ORA-VALIDATE-001, ORA-EDIT-001, ORA-ASSET-001, ORA-CONTAINER-001, ORA-STACK-001; 14 promoted to implemented, 1 (transactional CRUD) stays honestly partial with a precise, individually-verified characterization replacing the generic placeholder.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 6 obligations sharing one identical rule_text ('the required stack.xml archive member is a UTF-8 encoded XML document') closed via 2 new tests plus existing conformance/round-trip tests. 4 obligations sharing another identical rule_text ('full baseline support for reading/editing/viewing... editing may damage the result') closed via existing LOSSLESS/CANONICAL PreservationMode tests. 4 obligations with distinct claims closed individually (1 via cross-file citation to existing preservation tests, 1 via cross-file citation to existing round-trip tests, 1 via existing tree-structure tests plus 2 new root-constraint tests, 1 via 1 new vendor-archive-member-survival test). 1 obligation (transactional add/replace/move/rename/remove) stays partial: only add is genuinely tested; replace/move/remove/groups/metadata/reference-maintenance/stale-view-invalidation are not.

execution_steps: 1. Delegated initial per-obligation research to an Explore subagent covering all 15 non-empty-citation obligations, instructed to read every currently-cited test function's FULL body, confirm shipped-namespace imports, grep the actual source symbols, and search the whole ora test suite for better-fitting existing tests -- explicitly told to be skeptical since several citations looked like cross-capability copy-paste errors.

2. The subagent confirmed several definite mis-citations (a 'stack.xml is UTF-8 XML' claim cited against PNG-header tests with zero relation; the same claim cited against in-memory-only transaction tests that never serialize to stack.xml bytes; container.py's presence-only check cited as if it validated stack.xml content, when the real conformance logic lives in the uncited stack_xml.py module) and one precisely-scoped partial (transactional CRUD: only 'add' is tested; replace/move/remove/groups/metadata/reference-maintenance/stale-view-invalidation are not, per the test file's own module docstring).

3. Independently verified every claim before trusting it: read stack_xml.py's parse_stack and lifecycle.py's _canonical_stack_xml/dumps directly, ran interactive Python snippets confirming ElementTree.fromstring raises on invalid UTF-8 inside a document declaring encoding="UTF-8" (caught and converted to OraValidationError), confirmed the writer always emits the literal UTF-8 XML declaration and .encode("utf-8")'s the whole document, and confirmed the 'exactly one root <stack>' constraint in parse_stack works correctly for both zero-root and multi-root cases despite having zero test coverage.

4. Recognized a legitimate, non-fabricated connection the subagent's literal-text search missed: the 4 obligations sharing 'full baseline support for reading and editing and viewing... baseline support for visualization where editing may damage the result' map directly onto this library's LOSSLESS-vs-CANONICAL PreservationMode design -- LOSSLESS is the safe-by-default read/edit/view path that never damages unmodeled content, CANONICAL is the explicit, caller-chosen 'baseline save' path that visibly regenerates only what the model holds, matching OpenRaster's documented full-vs-baseline implementation-level concept precisely. Wrote this reasoning explicitly into implemented_behavior rather than a vague claim, so it is auditable.

5. Wrote 2 new tests for the previously-untested UTF-8 claim (test_written_stack_xml_declares_and_uses_utf8_encoding, test_invalid_utf8_in_a_declared_utf8_stack_xml_is_refused) in test_obligation_lifecycle_and_write.py, verified interactively with a scratch script against the module's own STACK/archive/png helpers before adding them as real pytest functions.

6. Wrote 1 new test (test_an_unrecognized_archive_member_survives_every_preservation_mode) proving a vendor archive member this library has no model for at all survives round-trip in both preservation modes -- the genuine, real evidence for 'custom extensions remain safe for baseline consumers' applied to raster/archive assets rather than stack.xml attributes.

7. Wrote 2 new tests (test_an_image_with_no_root_stack_is_refused, test_an_image_with_multiple_root_stacks_is_refused) in test_obligation_stack_and_document.py, closing the one previously-untested clause (root-versus-non-root constraints) of the tree-modeling obligation whose other clauses (visual order, nesting, child kind) were already well-proven but never cited.

8. Ran ruff on both changed test files (clean), the full ora suite (288 passed, was 283) before writing any evidence claim, patched the evidence YAML (14 promotions plus 1 precise-partial rewrite), and ran the reconciler. No src/ files changed this slice -- test files and evidence YAML only -- so skills-first governance was correctly skipped.
